sections.name: Riot Infected
sections.card:
Summary: A riot-armoured infected whose front is immune to bullets and melee, so hit its back, or use fire, explosions or the chainsaw. It appears only in The Parish and Cold Stream, and in No Mercy and Dead Air when you play them in Left 4 Dead 2.
Weak points: Hit it from behind: shove it to stun it and step around it, or shove it off-centre so it spins and shows its back. Fire, explosions and the chainsaw still work from the front.
Looks like: An armoured guard in a helmet with a visor and a light blue (sometimes grey) uniform with a sheathed nightstick. The bands on its arm are reflective, so a flashlight picks them out.
Tips: Survivor bots cannot tell it from other infected and waste ammo shooting its front, and it is especially dangerous to an incapacitated player, who often cannot land a shot on its back from the floor. Avoid fighting it where it can crawl, because a crawling one cannot be shoved back.

sections.name: CEDA Worker Infected
sections.card:
Summary: An uncommon infected in a hazmat suit that resists fire and sometimes drops a bile bomb, with 150 health on Normal and above. You meet it in Dead Center's Hotel and Streets, on the No Mercy hospital's lower floors and in Rayford's industrial area in The Sacrifice.
Weak points: Its suit makes it resistant to fire: a Molotov does not set it alight and incendiary ammo does not ignite it, though the bullets still hit, and one left idle in a fire for a long time dies from the heat. Shoot it or hit it with a melee weapon.
Looks like: A hazmat suit with reflective patches, yellow or green, with dark blue and white ones in the No Mercy hospital. A bile bomb strapped to its side means it may drop one when killed.
Tips: Its corpse sometimes holds a bile bomb you can pick up. In the No Mercy hospital they supply almost all the bile in the campaign, though they seldom carry one.

sections.name: Clown Infected
sections.card:
Summary: A fairground clown found in the Dark Carnival campaign. When it spots survivors it charges, and its squeaky shoes call the infected nearby to join the attack. It has 150 health on Normal and above.
Weak points: It shares a common infected's general weaknesses, but is a bit tougher. Shoving it honks its nose, and after four honks in a row the next shove kills it. If you kill one at a distance, the infected following it stop and mill about for a moment, so shoot them then.
Looks like: Squeaky shoes and striped trousers (for example pink and blue, red and yellow, or blue and white), and a flower on its chest that sometimes squirts water.
Tips: A clown does not make the Director spawn more infected: it only stirs up the ones already nearby, and its pull has no effect during a horde attack. A tight group running from one direction behind a clown is easier to shoot than infected arriving from different directions.

sections.name: Mud Men
sections.card:
Summary: Mud-covered infected from Swamp Fever that sprint on all fours. They also lurk on The Last Stand's Junkyard map and in the No Mercy and Death Toll sewers.
Weak points: Treat them like common infected, but a bit tougher: 150 health on Normal and above, 50 on Easy. They sprint on all fours but stumble back on two feet when shoved.
Looks like: An infected much like a common one, coated in reflective mud. It runs low on all fours but staggers back upright when you shove it.
Tips: A pipe bomb thrown into the swamp pulls nearby mud men to it and kills them easily, and a bile bomb thrown in gathers them in one spot. Turning off gore in the game's settings also turns off the mud blinding.

sections.name: Worker Infected
sections.card:
Summary: Road Crew infected, also called Worker Infected, wear ear protection and fill Hard Rain. In Left 4 Dead 2 they also appear in No Mercy, Dead Air, The Sacrifice and The Last Stand.
Weak points: Handle them like common infected, but a bit tougher: 150 health on Normal and above, 50 on Easy. They cannot hear a pipe bomb through their ear protectors.
Looks like: A hard hat in yellow or white, ear protectors and a reflective vest, which stands out most in Hard Rain's storms.
Tips: A bile bomb that lands without hitting any infected does not draw them either: they go for the survivors instead, so aim it to hit several infected. They still react to a chainsaw's noise.

sections.name: Fallen Survivor
sections.card:
Summary: A rare uncommon infected with 1000 health that cannot be set on fire, usually runs away when shot and may drop items when killed. It lives in The Passing, plus the original game's No Mercy, Death Toll, Crash Course and The Last Stand since the Last Stand update.
Weak points: Kill it with one melee swing, an explosive round, the M60, or a headshot while it still stands idle; a Magnum body shot does 500 damage. A shove halts its escape for a moment, but shove fatigue forces a three-second wait that lets it flee again.
Looks like: A man in militia clothes whose shirt is blue, white or green. A boonie hat tops him, and three ammo belts hold a visible Molotov, pipe bomb, pills and first aid kit.
Tips: What it carries varies, sometimes just one Molotov, and it may drop the lot at random when killed. If it gets away it lingers a long while, and the Director often puts a new one in earlier on the map.

sections.name: Molotov cocktail
sections.card:
Summary: A throwable that covers a large area in flames for roughly 15 to 17 seconds, spreading as it burns. Any infected touching the fire burns, and common infected that charge into it burn up.
Uses: Throw it at a choke point as the horde arrives, because infected never dodge fire. On high difficulties keep one for the Tank, which cannot put itself out away from water and, on fire alone, lasts 75 seconds on Easy and Normal, 80 on Advanced, 85 on Expert.
Tips: Aim at the floor: it does not go off against a wall or when it strikes a special infected. Keep it off teammates, since an incapacitated one in the flames is hard to revive and, on Expert, even a healthy survivor can burn to death.

sections.name: Pipe bomb
sections.card:
Summary: A throwable bomb whose bright red light and loud beeping pull common infected toward it, going off 6 seconds after the throw. Its blast reaches only about three to four metres on Normal, yet a well-placed one can kill 20 or more.
Uses: Use it to clear a space where common infected are loosely gathered, save one for a big horde, or pull enemies off a teammate who is incapacitated or covered in bile. One is enough: only the first one thrown draws them.
Tips: It works worse in Left 4 Dead 2, where idle infected react slowly to it and some not at all. Throw it low, and push away infected that are already close or they attack instead of chasing it. Special infected and Worker Infected are not drawn to it, and a Witch or Tank near the blast can be stumbled but will not follow.

sections.name: First aid kit
sections.card:
Summary: The healing item for the primary slot. Using it takes five seconds on yourself or a teammate and leaves you unable to fight back, and it heals only 80 percent of what is missing, so nobody reaches full health.
Uses: On a survivor on their last incapacitation it heals them and resets the count. Once incapacitated a survivor keeps only 1 permanent health, so a kit then gives 80, and it also wipes out any extra health from pills.
Tips: Safe room cabinets and finales always stock kits, but on Expert you almost never find one mid-level. Adrenaline cuts the use time to three seconds. In Left 4 Dead 2 a defibrillator or ammo upgrade can take a kit's place.

sections.name: Defibrillator
sections.card:
Summary: A one-use device, new in Left 4 Dead 2, that brings a dead survivor back to life. Select it to see the nearest corpse glow faintly red, walk up to it and hold the attack button for three seconds.
Uses: A revived survivor returns with 50 permanent health, carrying only a secondary weapon, so their dropped gear has to be collected. Any survivor's body will do.
Tips: You cannot carry it together with a first aid kit. Expect about one a level, and the Director often puts one nearby when a survivor is close to dying. Someone who dies by losing their grip on a ledge cannot be revived, because they fall away.

sections.name: Pain pills and adrenaline shot
sections.card:
Summary: Two items for the temporary healing slot. Pain pills give 50 temporary health that slowly drains away, and the adrenaline shot, new in Left 4 Dead 2, gives 25 temporary health and a 15-second boost. Either can be handed to a teammate with the melee button.
Uses: Pills drain one temporary health every 3 seconds, so they last 150 seconds at most, and they also clear speed penalties while your total health is over 40. Adrenaline lasts 15 seconds: you run faster, shove without tiring, heal, revive, reload and switch faster, and neither the horde's slowing hits nor water slow you.
Tips: Using a first aid kit removes the extra health pills gave you. Adrenaline narrows your view and flattens the sound to mono, so telling where a noise came from gets hard.

sections.name: Grenade launcher
sections.card:
Summary: A single-shot primary weapon, new in Left 4 Dead 2, that lobs a slow grenade in an arc. Near the blast, common and weaker special infected die and the rest stumble, except Chargers and Tanks. Reloading is slow, it holds one grenade with 30 spare, and ammo piles cannot refill it.
Uses: A direct hit on a Tank does 1000 damage. It can also shake a special infected off a pinned teammate from range without hurting that teammate, and its shots are best saved for very big crowds or a spawned horde.
Tips: Friendly fire is mild on lower difficulties but a real threat on higher ones, so switch to a secondary weapon in tight spaces or when a horde is right in front of you. Because the grenade explodes on contact, aim at a hard surface near the target, or from above at the middle of a horde, and lead moving targets because it flies slowly.

sections.name: M60 machine gun
sections.card:
Summary: A special-tier machine gun, new in Left 4 Dead 2, with a 150-round belt and no reloading. Ammo piles cannot refill it, and once the belt is empty it is dropped and you go back to your secondary weapon.
Uses: One shot kills any common infected wherever it lands, even on Expert Realism, and there is no reloading. An ammo upgrade converts whatever is left in the belt into incendiary or explosive rounds, so it is the best gun for either upgrade.
Tips: Switch to your secondary weapon against small groups to save the belt for larger ones. Its accuracy matches the AK-47's, so it is poor at long range or on the move, and special ammo on a nearly empty M60 is wasted because it only converts what is left.

sections.name: Chainsaw
sections.card:
Summary: A special melee weapon for the sidearm slot, new in Left 4 Dead 2, that deals 1000 damage per second and kills a common infected in one hit wherever it lands. Its fuel cannot be refilled, so it eventually runs dry, but it burns none while idle.
Uses: Most special infected die in under half a second, and a Charger in just over; a Tank takes 3, 4, 6 or 8 seconds on Easy, Normal, Advanced and Expert. The chainsaw cuts you loose from a Smoker's tongue without careful aim or timing, which other melee weapons need.
Tips: It needs a long rev-up, so start it before a horde reaches you, and being pinned or knocked down drops it back to idle. Its noise draws nearby common infected, and its arc hurts teammates, enough to incapacitate one on Realism, so keep your distance from them. Tap the fire button against small groups to save fuel.

sections.name: Incendiary and explosive ammo
sections.card:
Summary: Two upgrades for any primary weapon in Left 4 Dead 2, incendiary and explosive, which turn up only a handful of times per campaign. Set one on the ground and each player can grab a single extra magazine of the special rounds.
Uses: Incendiary rounds set special and common infected alight, but CEDA workers, Jimmy Gibbs Junior and the Fallen Survivor will not burn, and a common infected dies in one hit. Explosive rounds burst on any surface, wipe out every common infected at once and stagger every special infected except the Tank.
Tips: Fire explosive rounds at point blank and you and nearby teammates take damage, badly so on Advanced and Expert. They also set off gas cans, propane tanks, fireworks and oxygen tanks. Using the other kind replaces the active one, because they do not stack.
